title: When police may arrest without warrant
description: Police officer may arrest without an order from a Magistrate and without a warrant any person who has been concerned in any cognizable offence, or against whom a reasonable complaint has been made or credible information received.

title: Search for persons wrongfully confined
description: Magistrate may issue a search-warrant for search of any person confined under such circumstances that the confinement amounts to an offence.

title: Security for keeping the peace in other cases
description: Executive Magistrate may require a person likely to commit a breach of the peace or disturb public tranquility to execute a bond with or without sureties.

title: Power to issue order in urgent cases of nuisance or apprehended danger (Section 144)
description: Executive Magistrate may direct any person to abstain from a certain act or take certain order with respect to certain property to prevent danger to human life, health, safety, or riot.

title: Procedure where dispute concerning land, etc., is likely to cause breach of peace
description: Magistrate investigates possession of disputed land or water to prevent immediate bloodshed or violence.

title: Information in cognizable cases (First Information Report - FIR)
description: Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence given orally to an officer in charge of a police station shall be reduced to writing and signed by the informant.

title: Examination of witnesses by police
description: Police officer investigating may examine orally any person supposed to be acquainted with the facts and circumstances of the case.

title: Power to record statements and confessions
description: Metropolitan Magistrate or Magistrate of the first class may record any confession or statement made to him in the course of an investigation.

title: Procedure when investigation cannot be completed in twenty-four hours (Police Remand)
description: Accused forwarded to Magistrate; Magistrate may authorize detention in police custody (remand) not exceeding fifteen days in whole.

title: Report of police officer on completion of investigation (Charge Sheet / Final Report)
description: Final police report stating whether an offence appears to have been committed and by whom.

title: In what cases bail to be taken (Bailable offences)
description: When any person other than a person accused of a non-bailable offence is arrested, he shall be released on bail as a matter of right.

title: When bail may be taken in case of non-bailable offence
description: Court may grant bail in non-bailable cases, provided that a person shall not be released if there appear reasonable grounds for believing that he has been guilty of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, unless such person is under sixteen years of age, sick, infirm, or a woman.

title: Power to direct admission to bail or reduction of bail (Anticipatory Bail)
description: The High Court Division or Court of Session may direct that any person be admitted to bail, including anticipatory bail before actual arrest.

title: Saving of inherent power of High Court Division
description: Nothing in this Code shall be deemed to limit or affect the inherent power of the High Court Division to make such orders as may be necessary to give effect to any order under this Code, or to prevent abuse of the process of any Court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice (Quashment of criminal proceedings).
